pr_title: Permit 'R'/'r' format specifier with integer formatting
pr_body:
Treat it just like 'G'/'g'.  This is to minimize differences in numerical format allowances, primarily in support of generic math.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/67623

issue_context.title: Making numerical formatting specifiers more consistent
issue_context.body:
Today 'R'/'r' aren't supported with integral types but are with floating point, and 'X'/'x' aren't supported with floating point but are with integral types.  Related to both https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65634 and the generic math support, where `INumber<T>` inherits `ISpanFormattable` and thus we should expect format specifiers to be used with arbitrary numerical types, we should allow all of these specifiers to be used, regardless of integer vs floating point.  'R'/'r' for integers can just be treated as 'G'/'g', respectively, and 'X'/'x' for floating point is covered by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1630.

(Discussed in API review on 4/5/2022.)

cc: @tannergooding

This one should be relatively straightforward for `R`, it just needs to be treated the same as `G` for the built-in Integer types.

The hexadecimal support for floating-point types is a bit more complex (namely due to handling a different set of suffixes) but is tracked by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1630.

review_comments:
Hmmm. Preventing this seems wrong and inconsistent with what `UTF16` formatting does. (`5.ToString("G99")` is valid)

The official docs (https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/standard-numeric-format-strings) cover that it produces `Result: The more compact of either fixed-point or scientific notation` and `Precision specifier: Number of significant digits.`

There are notably some other inconsistencies here as well. Integers are missing support for `C`, `E`, `F`, and `P`. `Floating-point` more broadly doesn't support `D` either, but reasonably could (its basically just an alternative to `F0`)

-- Noting this is existing and I don't think this PR needs to address it, just calling it out as something else that might need broader consideration.

I didn't realize the UTF8 formatter was "so limited" compared to the UTF16 one.
Thanks.  Mind opening a separate issue to track that then?  It sounds like it's something we should address (at some point).
